findings.question: How does the extension start and connect?
findings.conclusion: MV3 module background worker registers its message listener before guarded startup steps, restores clickyTabs from session storage, persists a local profileId, connects to com.heyclicky.browser and sends hello protocol1. A 0.5-minute alarm plus startup/install events retries connect.

findings.question: How do app commands become browser results?
findings.conclusion: Native port ready messages update selected/reachable status. command messages call bridge.execute, then ModelView.forModel, then post a result or error with the same id. stop messages end active access. The command branch itself does not test connected; app/host selection and command admission need native-side corroboration.
remaining_unknowns: Native helper IPC from host to main app, selected-profile enforcement and app-generated command schema are not established by this JS source pass.

findings.question: Which browser operations exist?
findings.conclusion: The source contains 24 operation names, enumerated in source_ast_facts.browser_operations. Ordinary page actions are converted to a one-step batch with a final snapshot; explicit batches validate 1..20 steps before execution, serialize work per tab and stop after first failure/loading/dialog.

findings.question: How are jobs, turns and tabs owned?
findings.conclusion: Tasks own cancellation and per-turn cleanup while owner/thread identities own tabs, groups and kept state across turns. Claims move user tabs into job groups and restore their previous placement if the user has not since moved them. New tabs open unfocused near existing user/job tabs; cleanup preserves front tabs, moved-out tabs and explicit result/waiting keeps. Session storage persists only owned/homes/kept arrays. Stop hands owned tabs to the user instead of closing them.

findings.question: How does the model see the page and keep references?
findings.conclusion: Chrome Accessibility.getFullAXTree supplies nodes. Bounded snapshots prioritize reachable controls and nearby content, assign monotonically increasing eN refs to backendDOMNodeIds, and retire references on document epochs. ModelView turns nodes into text lines and returns added/removed deltas when at least half is retained and change size fits its threshold. Queries/interactive subsets never replace the full-page comparison baseline.

findings.question: What guards and observation limits are implemented?
findings.conclusion: Only credential-free HTTP(S) URLs are admitted, private tabs and tabs held by another running owner are refused. Debugger attachment uses protocol1.3; commander rechecks URL, task and epoch before every command. Fill rejects password/OTP/card autofill targets, typed input checks focused password fields, and javascript separately accepts arbitrary caller code up to20000 characters. These local guards do not prove a complete authorization policy.
remaining_unknowns: All guards describe visible code paths, not a proven global browser security policy. Native caller checks and actual browser behavior remain unobserved.

findings.question: How do downloads, uploads and text extraction work?
findings.conclusion: Downloads use Chrome downloads APIs and task-scoped sanitized names, track completion/danger/interruption and report deferred results. Uploads accept1..10 absolute paths and set DOM file inputs or intercept a chooser. Extract returns bounded main-frame markdown-like text and CSV tables while skipping form values and iframe content; snapshots alone create action refs.
remaining_unknowns: The native caller claim that paths were checked cannot be verified from extension code.

findings.question: How are connection and job status presented?
findings.conclusion: Background maps state to working/connected/profile/offline/setup/checking and updates toolbar icon, title and badge. Popup polls once per second with a1500ms response deadline, marks two consecutive misses stalled, shows up to three job cards, links tabs and supports Stop/open-app/reload actions. Cursor preference is persisted locally. Source CSS defines a280px black panel with paper-colored cards, aqua gel buttons and reduced-motion alternatives.
remaining_unknowns: No rendered popup or actual interaction was captured; extension CSS comments referring to native design do not establish pixel identity with the app.

findings.question: How is the browser cursor rendered?
findings.conclusion: A best-effort main-frame isolated world runs a generated presence function. It creates a closed-shadow zero-size fixed aria-hidden host with pointer-events:none and z-index2147483647, an edge glow, a16px triangle tilted-35deg and a grey11px progress bubble. Text streams by punctuation-aware timing; reduced-motion/hidden pages show it immediately. Screenshots temporarily hide presence. Runtime.createIsolatedWorld failure falls back to a missing contextId, so isolation is not unconditional.

findings.question: What interface connects the drawing engine to native painting?
findings.conclusion: The JS adapter implements a small SVG-like DOM, records dirty units/removals/structural wraps/property and motion patches, and __drainRender serializes operations in dependency/paint order. Text/path measurements, scheduling and time call __host members. The source declares native rendering ownership flags for pointers/buttons/windows/marquee.
remaining_unknowns: Actual JavaScriptCore context construction and native consumption of __drainRender operations are not traced here. Source comments name Core Animation/Core Text and candidate classes but do not prove that runtime path.

findings.question: How do speech and streaming drawing synchronize?
findings.conclusion: beginStream configures ClickyDraw.live with speech external and stream state; feed updates complete parsed statements and returns analyzed lines/actions. line and lineLength send externally supplied speech timing into engine lines. Buttons wait until their beat marks finish, then HOST.buttonReady receives the remaining delay. Drawing sounds and captions are emitted as typed host calls.
remaining_unknowns: Who supplies speech timestamps and how native audio/caption/button implementations consume them still needs native tracing.

findings.question: What drawing and card actions are exported?
findings.conclusion: The adapter exposes22 clickyCanvas methods. It supports continued turns, current-card text state, clear/finished/timeline, retaining notes or dropping screen pointers after screen changes, card move/zoom/close, button placement avoiding text, mark boxes,3D ticks and whole-program rendering. The3D tick output uses14 Float32 numbers per part with a set-field bitmask; thrown ticks stop, and ticks exceeding8ms more than five times stop.
remaining_unknowns: Native input handlers, card layering, actual Metal rendering and exhaustive ClickyDraw engine geometry/piece semantics were not recovered in this pass.
